mainTopic: משנה of הרואה (ברכות נד.): ברכות on sights, events, and news, along with related prayers and תקנות; the גמרא on blessing over public and private miracles
overview: This amud opens the ninth פרק of ברכות with one long משנה about ברכות said in response to things we see, hear, or experience. These include places of נסים, places where עבודה זרה was removed, powerful forces of nature, great features of creation, rain and good news, bad news, and new houses or כלים. The משנה teaches that one must bless ה׳ for bad things just as for good things, and it learns this from ״ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך״. It also rules that praying to change something that already happened is a תפלת שוא, and it gives the prayers for entering and leaving a כרך. It then lists rules of respect for הר הבית, the תקנה to close blessings with ״מן העולם ועד העולם״, and the תקנה to greet others using ה׳'s name. The גמרא then asks for the source of the ברכה over a נס, and רבי יוחנן brings it from יתרו. Stories about individuals who blessed over their personal miracles lead to the rule that a public miracle obligates everyone, while a private miracle obligates only the person it happened to. A ברייתא then lists famous places of miracles, and the גמרא begins to find a source for the miracle at the streams of ארנון. That story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blessing at a place where miracles happened
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the פרק: someone who sees a place where נסים were done for ישראל says a ברכה thanking ה׳ for those miracles.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who sees a place where miracles were done for ישראל says: 'Blessed… Who performed miracles for our forefathers in this place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins a new פרק about ברכות said in reaction to things we see or experience. The first case is seeing a place where a נס happened to ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברכה has no set time. Seeing the place is what creates the obligation. The wording 'לאבותינו' shows that we thank ה׳ even for נסים that happened to earlier generations.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sees
a place where miracles were done for Israel,
recites: 'Blessed… Who performed miracles'
for our forefathers in this place.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָרוֹאֶה מָקוֹם שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בּוֹ נִסִּים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of a new פרק and משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing a place of נסים for ישראל requires the ברכה 'שעשה נסים לאבותינו במקום הזה'.

steps.title: Blessing at a place where idolatry was uprooted
steps.stepSummary: Someone who sees a place from which עבודה זרה was removed thanks ה׳ for uprooting it from our land.
steps.simpleTranslation: A place from which idolatry was uprooted, one says: 'Blessed… Who uprooted idolatry from our land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second place-based ברכה. This one is for a spot where עבודה זרה used to be and is now gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first ברכה, it is triggered by seeing a meaningful place. Here the thanks is for a spiritual victory, the removal of עבודה זרה, and not for a physical rescue.

phrases.english: A place from which idolatry was uprooted,
one recites: 'Blessed… Who uprooted'
idolatry from our land.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case in the list of place-based ברכות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing a place where עבודה זרה was uprooted requires the ברכה 'שעקר עבודה זרה מארצנו'.

steps.title: Blessing over powerful forces of nature
steps.stepSummary: For dramatic natural events (זיקין, זוועות, thunder, winds, lightning) one says 'שכחו וגבורתו מלא עולם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For זיקין, for earthquakes, for thunder, for winds, and for lightning, one says: 'Blessed… Whose strength and power fill the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from special places to powerful events in nature. It gives one ברכה for all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these events show ה׳'s raw power, so the ברכה praises His כח and גבורה. The exact meaning of זיקין and זוועות is explained later in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A sky phenomenon, explained later in the גמרא (often understood as comets or shooting stars)

phrases.english: For zikin and for earthquakes,
and for thunder, and for winds,
and for lightning, one recites:
'Blessed… Whose strength and power fill the world.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from places to natural phenomena
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dramatic displays of nature's power require 'שכחו וגבורתו מלא עולם'.

steps.title: Blessing over great features of creation
steps.stepSummary: For mountains, hills, seas, rivers, and deserts one says 'עושה בראשית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For mountains, for hills, for seas, for rivers, and for deserts, one says: 'Blessed… Who makes the work of creation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists large, lasting parts of the natural world. It gives them their own ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step was about sudden events that show ה׳'s power. This step is about permanent features that show ה׳ as the Creator. So the ברכה here praises מעשה בראשית.

keyTerms.meaning: Who makes the work of creation

phrases.english: For mountains and for hills,
and for seas, and for rivers,
and for deserts, one recites:
'Blessed… Who makes the work of creation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel category: permanent creation instead of sudden power
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great natural landscapes require 'עושה בראשית'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's special blessing for the Great Sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that seeing הים הגדול gets its own ברכה, 'שעשה את הים הגדול', said only when one sees it occasionally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One who sees the Great Sea says: 'Blessed… Who made the Great Sea', when he sees it only from time to time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds his own view. The Great Sea is special enough to get its own ברכה, instead of the general 'עושה בראשית'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא included all seas under 'עושה בראשית'. רבי יהודה singles out הים הגדול. He also adds a condition: the ברכה is said only when one sees it 'לפרקים', at intervals, and not when it is a regular daily sight. The גמרא later explains how long that interval is.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who disagrees and gives a special ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think you must say this ברכה every time you look at the sea. The condition 'לפרקים' means only when you see it after a break.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who sees the Great Sea recites:
'Blessed… Who made the Great Sea' —
when he sees it at intervals.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אוֹמֵר: הָרוֹאֶה אֶת הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dissenting view that singles out one item from the previous list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, הים הגדול gets its own ברכה, said only when seen occasionally.

steps.title: Blessing for rain and good news
steps.stepSummary: For rain and good news one says 'הטוב והמטיב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For rain and for good news, one says: 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves from what we see to what we hear and receive. Rain and good news get the ברכה of thanks 'הטוב והמטיב'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain is placed together with good news because both are blessings that come to a person from ה׳. The גמרא later discusses when exactly this ברכה is said, especially for rain.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is good and does good

phrases.english: For rain and for good tidings
one recites: 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from seeing nature to receiving good events
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain and good news require 'הטוב והמטיב'.

steps.title: Blessing for bad news
steps.stepSummary: Even for bad news one says a ברכה: 'דיין האמת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For bad news, one says: 'Blessed is the true Judge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the matching ברכה for bad news. A person still blesses ה׳, accepting that His judgment is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the previous step. Good news gets 'הטוב והמטיב', and bad news gets 'דיין האמת'. Saying a ברכה over bad news expresses acceptance of ה׳'s judgment.

phrases.english: For bad tidings, one recites:
'Blessed is the true Judge.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror case to good news
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bad news requires 'דיין האמת'.

steps.title: Blessing for a new house or new vessels
steps.stepSummary: One who builds a new house or buys new כלים says 'שהחיינו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who built a new house or bought new vessels says: 'Blessed… Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ברכה for getting something new and personal. That ברכה is שהחיינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These ברכות are not about seeing nature or hearing news. They are about personal joy from a new acquisition. שהחיינו thanks ה׳ for letting us reach this happy moment.

phrases.aramaic: בָּנָה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ, וְקָנָה כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: One who built a new house or bought new vessels
recites: 'Blessed… Who has given us life,'
'sustained us, and brought us to this time.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּנָה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ, וְקָנָה כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the ברכה for new personal acquisitions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new house or new כלים requires שהחיינו.

steps.title: General rule: bless for bad as for good
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states a principle: one blesses on bad things just as on good things, and on good things just as on bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: One blesses over the bad just as over the good, and over the good just as over the bad.
steps.whatsHappening: After the specific ברכות, the משנה gives a general rule about attitude. A person must bless ה׳ for whatever happens now, good or bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something bad may later turn out well. Even so, a person says 'דיין האמת' now, based on how it looks at the moment. Something good may later bring trouble, yet a person still says 'הטוב והמטיב' now. The גמרא later also understands this as accepting bad things בשמחה, just as one accepts good things.
steps.whatToRemember: A Jew blesses ה׳ for everything, good and bad. Each ברכה is chosen according to how the event looks right now.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle shapes the Jewish attitude toward suffering. Bad things are also from ה׳ and are accepted with a ברכה.

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה מֵעֵין עַל הַטּוֹבָה,
phrases.english: One blesses over the bad just as over the good,
and over the good just as over the bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה מֵעֵין עַל הַטּוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizing principle for the good and bad ברכות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must bless for bad as for good, according to the present situation.

steps.title: Praying about the past is a useless prayer
steps.stepSummary: Crying out to change something that already happened is a תפלת שוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who cries out over the past, that is a vain prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new topic, prayers that are pointless. This line is the general rule, and the next two steps give examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Prayer is for asking about what is still open. Praying to change a fact that is already settled is called a 'vain' prayer, because one is asking ה׳ to undo reality.

phrases.english: And one who cries out over the past —
this is a vain prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: limits of prayer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying to change the past is a תפלת שוא.

steps.title: Example: praying for a boy when the wife is already pregnant
steps.stepSummary: Praying that one's pregnant wife will give birth to a boy is a תפלת שוא, since the baby's gender is already set.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his wife was pregnant and he says, 'May it be Your will that my wife gives birth to a boy', that is a vain prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first example of praying about the past. The baby already exists, so its gender is already decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer sounds like it is about the future birth. In truth it asks to change something already fixed. The גמרא later discusses whether there is a short early window when such a prayer could still work.

phrases.english: If his wife was pregnant, and he says:
'May it be Your will that my wife give birth to a male' —
this is a vain prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First illustration of the general rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying for the gender of an already-conceived child is a תפלת שוא.

steps.title: Example: praying the scream is not from my house
steps.stepSummary: Hearing a scream in the city and praying it is not from one's own home is a תפלת שוא, since whatever happened has already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was coming on the road and heard a scream in the city, and he says, 'May it be Your will that this is not in my house', that is a vain prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second example, and it closes the topic of תפלת שוא. The event behind the scream has already taken place, so praying about where it happened cannot change it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This example is clearer than the first, since the event is plainly over. Together the two examples define a תפלת שוא: a prayer about an outcome that is already fixed, even if the person does not yet know it.
steps.whatToRemember: A תפלת שוא is a prayer about something that is already decided. The person may not know the result yet, but it is already fixed.

phrases.english: If he was coming on the road
and heard the sound of a scream in the city, and he says:
'May it be Your will that this not be in my house' —
this is a vain prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה בָּא בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְשָׁמַע קוֹל צְוָחָה בָּעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second illustration of the general rule; closes the תפלת שוא section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying that an event that already occurred did not happen to one's household is a תפלת שוא.

steps.title: Two prayers when entering a big city
steps.stepSummary: Someone who enters a כרך says two prayers: one going in and one going out.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who enters a big city prays twice: once when he goes in and once when he leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule: going into a big, dangerous city calls for a prayer on the way in and another on the way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרך was a large walled city where a traveler could be in danger, for example from the government. So he asks for safety going in, and asks to leave safely. The opening rule counts two prayers in total.

keyTerms.meaning: A large walled city, often a dangerous place for a visitor

phrases.english: One who enters a large city recites two prayers,
phrases.notes: The גמרא later explains this is where entering is dangerous.

phrases.english: one when he enters, and one when he leaves.
phrases.notes: He asks to enter in peace and to leave in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of useless prayer (תפלת שוא) to a new case of a proper, useful prayer for safety.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Entering a כרך requires two prayers: one on entering and one on leaving.

steps.title: בן עזאי says four prayers
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי says four prayers: two going in and two going out. The extra ones are thanks for the past and a request for the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: four prayers, two when he enters and two when he leaves. He gives thanks for what already happened and cries out for what is still to come.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי disagrees with the first opinion and adds two more prayers. Each time, the person also thanks הקב״ה for getting him safely this far and asks for help with what lies ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree on praying for safety. בן עזאי adds that at each stage there is a past part (thanks) and a future part (request). This fits the earlier lesson: you thank for what already happened, and you only request what has not happened yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties back to the תפלת שוא idea from steps 10–12. Requests belong only to the future, and the past calls for thanks.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says: four,
two when he enters, and two when he leaves.
He gives thanks for what has passed
phrases.notes: Thanks for having arrived (or having left) safely.

phrases.english: and cries out for the future.
phrases.notes: A request for safety in what is still ahead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 13 about how many prayers are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי: four prayers. At entering and at leaving, one thanks for the past and one asks for the future.

steps.title: Bless for bad just as for good, with a verse as the source
steps.stepSummary: A person must bless הקב״ה for bad things just as for good things. The source is ״ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך בכל לבבך״.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person is obligated to bless over the bad just as he blesses over the good, as it says: 'And you shall love ה׳ your God with all your heart, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a firm obligation to bless over bad news and brings a פסוק as its source. The next steps explain how this פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 already said one blesses over bad as over good. Here the משנה itself repeats the idea, now as a חיוב (obligation), and attaches a Torah source. Loving הקב״ה ״בכל לבבך״ means loving Him in every situation, including painful ones.

keyTerms.meaning: The bad, something painful that happens
And you shall love (from קריאת שמע)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a pointless repeat of step 9. The משנה really does restate the principle here, this time to give its Torah source.

phrases.english: A person is obligated to bless over the bad
just as he blesses over the good,
as it is said: 'And you shall love ה׳ your God'
'with all your heart, etc.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (the verse is used as a source)
steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ עַל הַטּוֹבָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the principle of step 9 as an obligation and adds a scriptural source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must bless הקב״ה over bad events just as over good ones, based on ״ואהבת״.

steps.title: Explaining heart, soul, and might
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains each part of the פסוק: ״לבבך″ means both יצרים, ״נפשך״ means even if He takes your life, and ״מאדך״ means all your money.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With all your heart' means with both your inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination. 'With all your soul' means even if He takes your life. 'With all your might' means with all your money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now reads the פסוק phrase by phrase, showing that love of הקב״ה must be complete in every area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double ב in ״לבבך״ (instead of ״לבך״) hints at two hearts, meaning the יצר טוב and the יצר הרע. ״נפשך״ teaches love even when facing death. ״מאדך״ (literally 'your very much') is read as money. Each one shows love that continues even through loss and hardship.

keyTerms.meaning: Your 'might', read here as your money

phrases.english: 'With all your heart': with your two inclinations,
phrases.notes: Learned from the doubled ב in לבבך.

phrases.english: with the good inclination and with the evil inclination.
'And with all your soul':
even if He takes your soul.
'And with all your might': with all your money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the verse cited in step 15 to show how it supports blessing over bad.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Love of הקב״ה must include both inclinations, one's very life, and all one's money.

steps.title: Another reading: thank Him for every measure
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of ״בכל מאדך″: for every measure (מדה) הקב״ה gives you, thank Him (מודה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'with all your might' means for every single measure that He measures out to you, thank Him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה offers a different way to read ״מאדך״, through wordplay on מאד, מדה, and מודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading speaks most directly to the rule of blessing over bad. Whatever 'measure' הקב״ה deals you, good or bad, you thank Him for it. It is the clearest link between the פסוק and the obligation in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure, the way one is treated

steps.whatToRemember: The obligation to bless over bad comes from loving הקב״ה completely. That means with both inclinations, with your life, with your money, and with thanks for every measure He gives.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'with all your might':
with every single measure
that He measures out to you,
be thankful to Him.
phrases.notes: It's a play on words: מאד sounds like מדה and מודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative reading of ״בכל מאדך״ to the one in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thank הקב״ה for every measure He deals out, whether good or bad.

steps.title: No light-headed behavior facing the eastern gate
steps.stepSummary: One may not act lightly or disrespectfully opposite שער המזרח, because it lines up with the בית קדשי הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should not act lightheadedly opposite the Eastern Gate, which is directly aligned with the Holy of Holies.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shifts to a new subject: rules of respect connected to the מקדש. The first rule is not to act frivolously opposite the eastern gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eastern gate of הר הבית lined up straight with the בית קדשי הקדשים. Even outside the gate, acting frivolously facing it shows disrespect for the holiest place.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern gate of הר הבית

steps.confusionAlert: ״יקל את ראשו״ is an idiom for frivolous, disrespectful behavior. It is not about physically lifting or lightening one's head.

phrases.english: A person may not act lightheadedly
opposite the Eastern Gate
which is aligned directly opposite
the Holy of Holies.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יָקֵל אָדָם אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ כְּנֶגֶד שַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: respect for the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No frivolous behavior facing שער המזרח, since it aligns with the בית קדשי הקדשים.

steps.title: Respect on the Temple Mount: no stick, shoes, shortcuts, or spitting
steps.stepSummary: One may not enter הר הבית with a stick, shoes, a money belt, or dust on his feet. One may not use it as a shortcut (קפנדריא), and spitting is forbidden by קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not enter the Temple Mount with his staff, his shoes, his money belt, or with dust on his feet. He may not make it a shortcut. And spitting is forbidden all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists more ways to show respect on הר הבית. It ends by deriving the ban on spitting with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item treats הר הבית like an ordinary place: walking around with everyday gear, or cutting through it on the way somewhere else. The גמרא later builds the קל וחומר from shoes. Wearing shoes is not in itself a disgrace, yet the Torah forbade it in a holy place (״של נעליך״). So spitting, which is plainly disgraceful, is surely forbidden.

phrases.english: And he may not enter the Temple Mount
with his staff, his shoes, or his money belt,
or with the dust on his feet.
And he may not make it a shortcut.
And spitting is forbidden by an 'all the more so' argument.
phrases.notes: The גמרא learns this from shoes: if shoes, which are not disgraceful, are forbidden, spitting surely is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rules of respect for the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No entering הר הבית with a stick, shoes, money belt, or dusty feet. No using it as a shortcut. Spitting is forbidden by קל וחומר.

steps.title: Temple blessings originally ended with "until the world"
steps.stepSummary: In the מקדש, the closing of every blessing used to say ״עד העולם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: All those who concluded blessings in the Temple used to say 'until everlasting (the world).'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the original wording used to close blessings in the מקדש. This sets up the next step, which explains why the wording was changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש people did not answer אמן. They used a longer closing formula, and its ending was ״עד העולם״. This is background for the תקנה in the next step.

phrases.english: All who concluded blessings in the Temple
would say 'until everlasting (the world).'

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל חוֹתְמֵי בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, still connected to the מקדש: the wording of blessings there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, blessings in the מקדש closed with ״עד העולם״.

steps.title: Wording changed to "from the world to the world"
steps.stepSummary: When the מינין claimed there is only one world, the חכמים made a תקנה to say ״מן העולם ועד העולם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the heretics went astray and said there is only one world, they instituted that people should say 'from everlasting to everlasting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains why the closing wording was changed: to reject a false belief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying only ״עד העולם״ could be misread as speaking of a single world. Saying ״מן העולם ועד העולם״ names two worlds, this world and עולם הבא. The new wording publicly affirms belief in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: From the world to the world, affirming two worlds

steps.whatToRemember: The wording of a ברכה can be changed to fight false beliefs. ״מן העולם ועד העולם״ declares that there is both this world and עולם הבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the חכמים shaping the wording of prayer to protect core beliefs. This phrase is still found in our תפילות.

phrases.english: When the heretics went astray
and said there is only one world,
they instituted that people should say
'from everlasting to everlasting (from the world to the world).'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁקִּלְקְלוּ הַמִּינִין וְאָמְרוּ אֵין עוֹלָם אֶלָּא אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the change to the wording described in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the מינין denied עולם הבא, the חכמים instituted the closing ״מן העולם ועד העולם״.

steps.title: The חכמים instituted greeting with ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים instituted that a person greets his friend using ה׳'s name, as בועז did with the reapers.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also instituted that a person should ask about his friend's welfare using ה׳'s name. As it says: "And behold, בועז came from בית לחם and said to the reapers, 'ה׳ is with you,' and they answered him, 'May ה׳ bless you.'"
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another תקנה: when you greet someone, you may use ה׳'s name. It proves this from בועז greeting his workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think saying ה׳'s name in a casual greeting is not respectful. The משנה says the opposite: the חכמים made it a תקנה, and בועז, a great צדיק, already did it.

keyTerms.meaning: Greeting someone, asking about his welfare

phrases.english: And they instituted that a person should ask
about his fellow's welfare with the Name (of ה׳)
as it says: "And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem
and said to the reapers, ה׳ is with you
and they said to him, May ה׳ bless you."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם שׁוֹאֵל אֶת שְׁלוֹם חֲבֵרוֹ בַּשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of תקנות in the משנה, right after the תקנה of ״מן העולם ועד העולם״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may, and should, greet a friend using ה׳'s name.

steps.title: More verses supporting greeting with ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings three more פסוקים: the מלאך greeting גדעון, ״אל תבוז כי זקנה אמך״, and ״עת לעשות לה׳ הפרו תורתך״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: "ה׳ is with you, mighty warrior." And it says: "Do not scorn your mother when she is old." And it says: "It is a time to act for ה׳; they have voided Your תורה."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more פסוקים to strengthen the תקנה of greeting with ה׳'s name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might say בועז acted on his own, so the משנה shows that a מלאך greeted גדעון the same way. ״אל תבוז״ teaches: don't look down on this old custom of our fathers. ״עת לעשות לה׳״ answers the worry about using ה׳'s name casually: greeting people and making peace is doing ה׳'s will, so it is allowed even if it looks like a breach.

keyTerms.meaning: A time to act for ה׳

phrases.english: And it says: "ה׳ is with you, mighty warrior."
phrases.notes: שופטים ו:יב — the מלאך to גדעון

phrases.english: And it says: "Do not scorn your mother when she is old."
phrases.notes: משלי כג:כב — don't look down on old customs

phrases.english: And it says: "It is a time to act for ה׳;
they have voided Your Torah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds supporting פסוקים to the בועז proof of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The תקנה to greet with ה׳'s name
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מלאך's greeting to גדעון, ״אל תבוז״, and ״עת לעשות לה׳״

steps.title: רבי נתן reads the verse in reverse order
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן explains: "they voided Your תורה" because "it is a time to act for ה׳".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: "They voided Your תורה" because "it is a time to act for ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן gives his own reading of the same פסוק, reading the second half first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, the פסוק teaches a general rule: sometimes the חכמים must set aside a תורה rule, and they do it because the moment calls for acting for ה׳. It is the same idea seen from the other side: the breach is justified by the greater need.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who offers a second reading

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with the rule of ״עת לעשות לה׳״: when the hour demands it, the חכמים may set aside a rule in order to serve ה׳.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
"They voided Your Torah" because "it is a time to act for ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the last פסוק quoted in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting aside the תורה is sometimes done for the sake of acting for ה׳.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source of the miracle blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule: blessing when seeing a place where a miracle happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks where the משנה's rule comes from. It is setting up the next move, where רבי יוחנן gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "These things" means the first line of the משנה at the start of the פרק: someone who sees a place where miracles were done for ישראל says a ברכה. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows a ברכה is said for a miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is NOT about the greeting rule just mentioned. It goes back to the opening line of the משנה: the ברכה on a place of miracles.

phrases.english: Gemara:
From where are these matters (derived)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the end of the משנה back to its first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Scriptural source for saying a ברכה over a miracle.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: יתרו blessed ה׳ for the rescue
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings the source from יתרו, who said ״ברוך ה׳ אשר הציל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says, "And יתרו said: Blessed is ה׳, Who rescued..."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. יתרו blessed ה׳ for saving ישראל from מצרים, which shows we bless ה׳ for a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יתרו's words begin with ״ברוך״, the language of a ברכה, and they are said because of a rescue. That is the model for a ברכה on a miracle.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: For the verse says:
"And Jethro said, Blessed is ה׳
Who rescued, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is יתרו's blessing over the rescue of ישראל.

steps.title: Challenge: an individual saved from a lion was told to bless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether only a miracle for the many gets a ברכה, since רבא told a man saved from a lion to bless every time he passed that place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we bless only for a miracle of the many, and not for a miracle of an individual? But there was a man walking on the far side of the river. A lion attacked him, a miracle happened, and he was saved. He came before רבא, who told him: "Every time you come there, bless: 'Blessed is He Who did a miracle for me in this place.'"
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה (and the יתרו source) speak of miracles for all of ישראל. The גמרא challenges: does that mean an individual's miracle gets no ברכה? A story with רבא shows that it does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions ״נסים לישראל״, which sounds like it limits the ברכה to national miracles. But רבא told a private person to bless at the spot of his own rescue. So a ברכה is said for a personal miracle too, and the narrow reading is being attacked.

keyTerms.meaning: A miracle for the many (the public)
Who did a miracle for me in this place

phrases.english: For a miracle of the many we bless,
but for a miracle of an individual we do not bless?!
But there was a certain man
who was walking along the far side of the river (or: the right side).
A lion fell upon him,
a miracle was done for him and he was saved from it.
He came before Rava, and he said to him:
Every time you arrive there —
bless: "Blessed is He Who did a miracle for me
in this place."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנִּיסָּא דְרַבִּים מְבָרְכִינַן, אַנִּיסָּא דְיָחִיד לָא מְבָרְכִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implied limit, from the משנה and the יתרו source, that only public miracles get a ברכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that a ברכה on a miracle applies only to miracles for the many.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא told an individual to bless at the site of his private rescue, so individual miracles also get a ברכה.

steps.title: Second story: מר בריה דרבינא finds water in the desert
steps.stepSummary: The challenge continues with a second story: מר בריה דרבינא was thirsty and a spring of water was created for him by a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מר the son of רבינא was walking in a valley of willows and was thirsty for water. A miracle was done for him: a spring of water was created for him, and he drank.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second story of a private miracle to strengthen the challenge. Step 29 continues the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another case of a miracle for just one person, building the pile of evidence that individuals also bless over miracles. Step 29 gives the point of the story: he made a ברכה when he came to that spot.

phrases.english: And Mar, son of Ravina, was walking
in a valley of willows and was thirsty for water.
A miracle was done for him,
a spring of water was created for him, and he drank.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל בְּפַקְתָּא דַעֲרָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second example to the challenge of step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The same implied limit to public miracles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another private miracle, which the continuing story will show was also blessed over.

steps.title: Mar son of רבינא and the wild camel
steps.stepSummary: The challenge continues. A wall opened to save מר בריה דרבינא from a wild camel, and he made a ברכה at both of his miracle places.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: once he was walking in the marketplace of מחוזא and a wild camel attacked him. A wall cracked open for him, and he went inside it. When he came to the ערבות (the willows, where the spring miracle happened), he blessed: 'Blessed... Who did a miracle for me in the ערבות and with the camel.' When he came to the marketplace of מחוזא, he blessed: 'Blessed... Who did a miracle for me with the camel and in the ערבות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second personal miracle of מר בריה דרבינא. Again, a private person made a ברכה on his own miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה seemed to require a ברכה only for a miracle done for all of כלל ישראל. This story shows a ברכה even for a miracle done for one person. That makes the challenge stronger. Notice that at each place he mentions both of his miracles, starting with the miracle of the place where he is standing.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds another proof to the same challenge
Willows; the place of his earlier spring miracle

phrases.english: And furthermore, one time
he was walking in the marketplace of Meḥoza
and a wild camel attacked him.
A wall cracked open for him, and he went inside it.
phrases.notes: He was saved by hiding inside the wall.

phrases.english: When he came to the willows, he blessed:
'Blessed... Who performed a miracle for me
in the willows and with the camel.'
When he came to the marketplace of Meḥoza, he blessed:
'Blessed... Who performed a miracle for me
with the camel and in the willows!'
phrases.notes: This is still a question: here one person's miracle got a ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second miracle story of the same person to the challenge from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that only a miracle of the many requires a ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A private individual blessed on his personal miracles at each place, so a personal miracle must also require a ברכה.

steps.title: Miracle of the many versus miracle of one person
steps.stepSummary: For a miracle of the many, everyone must bless. For a miracle of an individual, only that individual must bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: On a miracle for the many, everyone is obligated to bless. On a miracle for an individual, he himself is obligated to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both kinds of miracles get a ברכה. The difference is only who has to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is talking about the ברכה that everyone says. That ברכה is only for a miracle of the many. A personal miracle also gets a ברכה, but only the person it happened to says it. So the stories of רבא and מר בריה דרבינא do not contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A miracle done for the many (the community)
A miracle done for one person

steps.whatToRemember: Every miracle gets a ברכה. For a miracle of the many, all people bless. For a miracle of an individual, only the person it happened to blesses. (Later sources say his descendants bless as well, but that is not in our text.)
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a personal miracle has no ברכה. It has one. Only the circle of people who must say it is smaller.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the practical הלכה for blessing on personal miracles.

phrases.english: They said: On a miracle of the many
everyone is obligated to bless,
on a miracle of an individual
he himself is obligated to bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in steps 27 to 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes who is obligated: the משנה refers to a ברכה that everyone says.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה speaks of miracles for כלל ישראל, it seemed that a personal miracle gets no ברכה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A miracle of the many obligates everyone. A miracle of an individual obligates only that individual.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists famous places of miracles
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists eight places of miracles where one who sees them must give thanks and praise to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One who sees the crossings of the sea, the crossings of the ירדן, the crossings of the streams of ארנון, the hailstones of אלגביש on the slope of בית חורון, the rock that עוג king of בשן wanted to throw on ישראל, the rock that משה sat on when יהושע fought עמלק, the wife of לוט, and the wall of יריחו that sank into the ground. On all of them, he must give thanks and praise to ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a list of miracles of the many. Seeing any of these places requires thanking ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list gives real examples of the משנה's rule about seeing a place of a miracle for ישראל. The next steps begin finding a source for these items, starting with the sea, the ירדן, and ארנון. The rest are discussed on the next amud. The wife of לוט is an unusual item, since it is a punishment and not a rescue. It is still listed.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים taught; introduces a ברייתא
Huge hailstones that fell in the war of יהושע

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who sees the crossings of the sea,
and the crossings of the Jordan, the crossings of the streams of Arnon,
the hailstones of Elgavish on the descent of Beit Ḥoron,
and the rock that wanted to throw
Og, king of Bashan, upon Israel,
phrases.notes: Read this with the line before: it's the rock Og wanted to throw on Israel.

phrases.english: and the rock on which Moses sat
when Joshua waged war against Amalek,
and Lot's wife,
and the wall of Jericho that was swallowed up in its place,
on all of them he must give
thanks and praise before God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining whose miracles get a ברכה, the גמרא lists the classic miracles of the many.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing any of these eight places of miracles requires giving thanks and praise to ה׳.

steps.title: The sea and the Jordan are clear, but where is ארנון?
steps.stepSummary: The crossings of the sea and the Jordan are clearly written in the verses. The גמרא asks for the source of a miracle at the streams of ארנון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable for the crossings of the sea, since it is written: 'And בני ישראל came into the middle of the sea on dry land.' And the crossings of the ירדן, since it is written: 'The כהנים carrying the ארון of ה׳'s covenant stood firm on dry land in the middle of the ירדן, and all ישראל crossed on dry land until the whole nation finished crossing the ירדן.' But the crossings of the streams of ארנון, where do we know it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first points out that two items on the list clearly have verses. Then it asks where we learn about a miracle at ארנון. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'it makes sense for these.' It grants the easy cases so the hard case stands out. The תנ״ך never openly describes a miracle at ארנון, so the גמרא wants a source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable for...; grants easy cases before asking about a hard one

phrases.english: Granted, the crossings of the sea, as it is written:
'And the Israelites came
into the midst of the sea on dry ground.'
The crossings of the Jordan, as it is written:
'The priests who carried the Ark of the covenant of God stood
on dry land in the middle of the Jordan, firmly,
and all Israel crossed on dry land
until the whole nation finished
crossing the Jordan.'
But the crossings of the streams of Arnon, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins finding sources for the items in the ברייתא of step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in תנ״ך for a miracle at the streams of ארנון

steps.title: The verse about the Book of the Wars of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The source for ארנון is the verse in במדבר about the 'Book of the Wars of ה׳: את והב בסופה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of ה׳: את והב בסופה, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from פרשת חוקת that mentions the wars of ה׳ near ארנון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the verse does not clearly describe a miracle. The גמרא will now bring a teaching that reads 'את והב בסופה' as hinting to a hidden miracle story.

keyTerms.meaning: The Book of the Wars of ה׳

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Therefore it is said
in the Book of the Wars of the Lord:
Et and Hev at the end, etc.'
phrases.notes: The next step explains these words as the names of two people at the end (סוף) of the camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״עַל כֵּן יֵאָמַר בְּסֵפֶר מִלְחֲמֹת ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'על כן יאמר בספר מלחמות ה׳ את והב בסופה' (במדבר 21:14) is the source.

steps.title: Two מצורעים at the back of the camp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains 'את והב בסופה' as two מצורעים walking at the end of the camp. The story begins as the אמוריים came.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'את והב בסופה': there were two מצורעים who were walking at the end of the camp of ישראל. When ישראל were passing through, the אמוריים came...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the strange words of the verse as a story. The story continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'את' and 'והב' are read as names of two people. 'בסופה' is read as 'at the end,' meaning the back of the camp. These two מצורעים are going to see the miracle at ארנון, so this explains why the verse is a source for the miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: People with צרעת, who had to stay outside the main camp

phrases.english: It was taught: 'Et and Hev at the end':
there were two lepers,
who were walking at the end of the camp of Israel.
When Israel were passing through,
the Emorites came
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the verse brought in step 33 so it shows a miracle at ארנון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'את והב בסופה' refers to two מצורעים walking at the end of the camp. The story of the miracle at ארנון begins when the אמוריים came as ישראל passed.
